short: The squares d4, e4, d5 and e5 — worth more than any others.
body: A piece in the centre touches more squares and can reach either wing quickly. A knight on d4 controls eight squares; the same knight on a1 controls two. Everything in the opening is a fight over these four squares.

There are two ways to control them. Occupying with pawns is the strongest and least flexible; attacking from a distance with pieces is more flexible and easier to undermine. Both count, and most openings do some of each.
Control matters more than occupation. A pawn on d4 that is attacked three times and defended twice is not control, it is a target.

diagram.caption: Every developed piece here points at the four central squares.
